title: Layer E: Implement draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00 (new jmap-chat-tasks-{types,server,client} crates)
description:
Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00.

NOT WORKED in the JMAP-v9py compliance sweep; filed for a later session.

Capability: urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:tasks (meaningful only with both urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat AND urn:ietf:params:jmap:tasks).

## Naming note

Workspace already has crate-jmap-tasks-* for the IETF draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06 binding. This bead's crates would be named crate-jmap-chat-tasks-* to disambiguate.

## What needs to land

- Space extension: taskListId (optional; same account; at most one TaskList per Space)
- Task extension: chatId (when mayBackReferenceChat advertised; back-reference to Chat)
- No new methods. Reuses JMAP Tasks methods.
- MessageAction "urn:jmap:chat:cap:task" semantics (uri forms, metadata keys: status, due, assigneeIds, priority)
- Lifecycle: destroying Task doesn't auto-destroy Chat; destroying Chat clears Task.chatId
- Cross-account validation (privilege-escalation risk)
- Capability fields: mayBindTaskList, mayBackReferenceChat

## Dependencies

- crate-jmap-tasks-types must be stable (IETF binding; workspace already has it)
- jmap-chat-types Space extension shape
notes:
2026-10-19 spec gap audit: children filed (types, taskListId patch, cascades, chatId rules, assigneeIds federation mapping). Depends on the chat extension seams epic; assigneeIds task depends on JMAP-v9py.15.
Crate placement decided 2026-10-20 (JMAP-v9py.16.8): binding crate-jmap-chat-<x>-server for cross-layer server rules; chat-object fields in chat-types; client helpers in chat-client unless they need the other layer's client.
